reason: The cited evidence (E1–E3) only defines HEAs and notes the need for improved high-temperature properties in single-phase alloys; none provides data on Ti–Ni primary HEAs, the effect of Al on γ′ formation in such systems, or the resulting mechanical behavior. The key premises are therefore unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Aluminum addition to a Ti–Ni primary HEA will induce a γ + γ′ dual-phase microstructure.
The γ′ precipitates will impede dislocation motion and stabilize the microstructure at elevated temperatures.
The dual-phase microstructure will improve elevated-temperature tensile strength and creep resistance.
The improvement is expected above ~700 °C within HEA compositional limits.
